name: what to compile first
hook: How does a build system know what to compile first? It sorts a graph.
hook_slide: How does a build system know what to compile *first*?
caption: To build a source file you must first build the modules it imports. Model each file as a vertex and each "A before B" as an edge A → B. A topological sort is an order in which every edge points forward.
Kahn's algorithm: anything with no unmet dependencies is safe to place. Place it, remove its edges, and whatever just dropped to zero dependencies is ready next.
Four files, four imports ({imports}) come out as {order}.
And the cycle check is free: make app a dependency of utils and {ready_in_cycle} of the {n} files can ever be built. The order comes up short, so no valid order exists.
Where else have you met this? Course prerequisites, spreadsheet cells… 👇
cta: Then the DFS version, and why only a DAG can be ordered.

slides.h: Tasks are vertices. "Before" is an edge.
p: To build a source file you must first build the modules it imports.
Draw A → B for "A must come before B". A *topological sort* is an order where every edge points forward.

slides.h: Start with what depends on nothing
p: A vertex with in-degree zero has no unmet dependencies, so it is safe to place first.
Place it, remove its edges, and whatever just dropped to zero is ready next.
The queue starts with every vertex whose in-degree is zero. Each one placed can free the vertices it points to.

slides.h: A cycle has no starting point

rows.lab: Make app a dependency of utils

p: A vertex on a cycle never reaches in-degree zero. If the order comes up short, no valid order exists.
